entries.3560cc5a96b212d9: This business manufactures and sells ham and sausages, processed foods, marine products and dairy products in Japan and overseas. In Japan, the company, Nippon Ham Factory Co., Ltd., Minami Nippon Ham Co., Ltd., Nippon Ham Foods Co., Ltd., Nippon Ham Sozai Co., Ltd. and others manufacture them, and the company, Nippon Ham Marketing Co., Ltd. and others sell them. Hoko Co., Ltd. and Nippon Luna Co., Ltd. handle marine products and dairy products. Overseas, Day-Lee Foods, Inc., Thai Nippon Foods Co., Ltd. and others manufacture and sell ham, sausages, processed foods and meat. In April 2025, the Overseas Business Division was abolished, and the overseas processing subsidiaries were transferred to this segment. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥448,366 million; revenue including internal revenue between segments was ¥530,339 million, a 0.6% decrease from the previous year. Manufacturing volume rose at the LJD Holdings group in North America, acquired in the previous fiscal year, but in the first half, sales volumes of various products other than Shauessen and the chilled bakery group declined, which had an impact.
entries.377e3d19598d3bfd: This business produces and sells meat, such as pork, chicken and beef, in Japan and overseas. In Japan, Nippon White Farm Co., Ltd. and Nippon Clean Farm Co., Ltd. raise pigs and broilers, Nippon Food Packer Co., Ltd. and others process them, and they are sold through the company and sales subsidiaries nationwide. Overseas, NH Foods Australia Pty. Ltd., Whyalla Beef Pty. Ltd. and others produce and sell meat. In April 2025, the Overseas Business Division was abolished, and the overseas meat subsidiaries were transferred to this segment. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥979,609 million, the largest among the reportable segments; revenue including internal revenue between segments was ¥1,034,133 million, an 8.1% increase from the previous year. The increase in revenue was due to improved sales conditions and higher sales volumes for domestic chicken and Australian beef, in addition to progress in passing on prices in the sales division.

entries.7e3d8599571de8fc: Domestically, meat, ham, sausages and processed foods are sold through the company and sales subsidiaries with sales bases nationwide (for meat: Higashi-Nihon Food Co., Ltd., Kanto-Nihon Food Co., Ltd., Naka-Nihon Food Co., Ltd. and Nishi-Nihon Food Co., Ltd.; for ham, sausages and processed foods: Nihon Ham Marketing Co., Ltd. and others). Revenue (excluding internal revenue between consolidated companies) for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥227,924 million for Kanto-Nihon Food Co., Ltd., ¥191,559 million for Naka-Nihon Food Co., Ltd. and ¥161,733 million for Nihon Ham Marketing Co., Ltd., and all 3 companies exceeded 10% of consolidated revenue. No customer accounts for 10% or more of revenue, and revenue by customer and customers' business types are not shown in the filing. Overseas, NH Foods Australia Pty. Ltd. and others sell meat. Customers of the Ballpark Business are professional baseball spectators and visitors to Hokkaido Ballpark F Village; visitors for the fiscal year ended March 2026 were 4.66 million (target: 4 million or more).
entries.80e3ddee2e219004: Profit attributable to owners of the parent for the fiscal year ended March 2026 (the amount corresponding to net income) was ¥35,066 million, up 31.9% from ¥26,585 million in the previous year.
entries.89af391572052bbd: This business organizes professional baseball games, operates the ballpark centered on “Hokkaido Ballpark F Village” in Kitahiroshima, Hokkaido, and oversees its overall management. It is made up of Hokkaido Nippon-Ham Fighters Co., Ltd., Fighters Sports & Entertainment Co., Ltd. and others. Revenue from external customers in the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥27,785 million; revenue including internal revenue between segments was ¥31,027 million, a 15.0% increase from the previous year. Team performance was strong and attendance reached a record high, and events held in the off-season brought ballpark visitors to 4.66 million, increasing revenue from tickets, merchandise, and food and beverages. In April 2026, the “Sports & Entertainment Business Division” was newly established, and this business came under its umbrella.
entries.8bf628992038b1d2: Revenue from tickets, merchandise and food and beverages of the Ballpark Business (external revenue of ¥27,785 million)
entries.8cb0d56de78b696b: Revenue for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was ¥1,457,391 million, up 6.3% year on year, mainly due to higher sales of Australian beef in the meat business and higher unit prices for domestically raised chicken. External revenue was ¥979,609 million for the Meat Business Division, ¥448,366 million for the Processing Business Division and ¥27,785 million for the Ballpark Business, and eliminations, adjustments and others amounted to ¥1,631 million. By location of the selling entity, Japan was ¥1,209,122 million (up 2.8% year on year) and other regions were ¥248,269 million (up 28.0% year on year, mainly due to higher meat sales prices). Revenue is recognized when products are delivered to customers and is measured at the amount after deducting rebates and discounts based on sales volume and sales amount.

entries.bc2b63a2fddd7077: In the Meat Business Division, Nihon White Farm Co., Ltd. and Nihon Clean Farm Co., Ltd. raise pigs and broilers, and Nihon Food Packer Co., Ltd. and others handle processing. Overseas, Whyalla Beef Pty. Ltd. and others raise cattle in Australia. In the Processing Business Division, the company, Nihon Ham Factory Co., Ltd. and others produce ham, sausages and processed foods, and Hōkō Co., Ltd. and Nihon Luna Co., Ltd. produce marine products and dairy products; overseas, Day-Lee Foods, Inc. (United States) and Thai Nippon Foods Co., Ltd. (Thailand) manufacture and sell products. In the Ballpark Business, Hokkaido Nihon-Ham Fighters Co., Ltd., Fighters Sports & Entertainment Co., Ltd. and others handle professional baseball events, stadium operation and overall management of the ballpark. The main brands are “Shaweissen” for ham and sausages, “Chūka Meina” for processed foods, and the branded meats “Sakurahime,” “Mugikomachi” and “Ōmugi-gyū ANGUS.” The branded beef ratio for the fiscal year ended March 2026 was 66.1%, exceeding the target of 60% (attributed to factors including the expansion of feedlots, or beef cattle fattening facilities).

entries.d459ac8c85cfb46d: NH Foods Ltd. forms a group consisting of the company, 65 [[term:subsidiary|subsidiaries]], 5 associates and 2 joint ventures, and its consolidated financial statements are prepared under [[term:ifrs|IFRS Accounting Standards]]. The businesses are managed as 3 [[term:segment|reportable segments]]: the Processing Business Division, the Meat Business Division and the Ballpark Business. In April 2025, the “Overseas Business Division” was abolished, and its overseas subsidiaries and associates were transferred to the Processing Business Division and the Meat Business Division. A feature of the group is that it handles everything consistently from production and rearing through processing and sales, and its products cover a wide range related to meat.
